decisions.reason: Same permission to read and study owned repository material, with the same ownership condition (lines 10–12).
Same permission to reference project ideas, patterns, and approaches (line 13).
Same permission to discuss the project publicly conditioned on attribution, including the same attribution obligation (line 14).
Same limited copying permission, purposes, attribution condition, and restriction against presenting the excerpt as one's own work (lines 15–17).

The current rule captures the introductory direct-written-permission exception and expressly limits it to the restrictions that follow, rather than treating it as a standalone prohibition (lines 21–28).
Same restriction on redistributing substantial portions absent direct written permission (lines 21, 23).
Same restriction on publishing a modified version or fork as a competing distribution absent direct written permission (lines 21, 24).
Same restriction on packaging, selling, sublicensing, or commercially exploiting repository content absent direct written permission (lines 21, 25).
Same restriction on offering the project or a substantial derivative as a hosted service absent direct written permission (lines 21, 26).
Same restriction on incorporating substantial portions into a commercial product absent direct written permission (lines 21, 27).
Same restriction on removing or obscuring the listed notices absent direct written permission (lines 21, 28).

Lines 32–34 express openness to broader arrangements and say permission may be granted case by case; they do not grant permission or create an operative permission clause. The candidate itself acknowledges that it is not a grant.

The operative local duty is prior discussion before contribution (lines 36–37), already represented by the current rule. The referenced CONTRIBUTING.md terms are not supplied, so no further terms can be extracted.

Lines 41–44 delimit this license to repository content owned by Rasmus Thornberg and state that separately licensed materials remain under their own licenses; they impose no standalone Use permission or restriction. The referenced THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md is not supplied, so its terms cannot be extracted.

Lines 48–50 identify the version to which the notice applies and speculate that future versions may have different terms; they grant no independent activity permission and impose no operative future-version duty.
